plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like lilac-pink flowers in autumn, without any leaves present. The leaves appear the following spring and die back by early summer. All parts of the plant are highly toxic due to colchicine.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in damp meadows and woodland edges; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicine from this plant is used in medicine to treat gout and by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling. The flowers are nicknamed 'naked ladies' because they bloom without leaves.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower with arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It forms dense colonies in meadows, roadsides, and fields, and provides vital late-season nectar and pollen for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: North America, in meadows, prairies, and roadsides; invasive in parts of Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and insect-carried; the true culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow flower balls. It blooms in late winter to spring in Australia and is a hardy species of dry woodlands and scrub.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, New South Wales, and South Australia
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An easy-to-grow annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall, slender stems. It thrives in full sun and poor soil and blooms prolifically until the first frost, attracting pollinators in autumn gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through fall (June to first frost)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated in gardens worldwide, with naturalized populations in many regions
plants.funFact: The name Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony, which was inspired by the orderly arrangement of its petals.
